header: An answer about SPECIFIC people has to say WHO each row is about. "Which department is ticket 228757 in" was answered with just Dept Code | Department 12000 | CO & CC (BATTERY) -- a department with no person: the reader cannot tell whose it is, and a name is what a ticket number is read against. So my rule: a lookup of specific people (a ticket number, or a name typed in the question) must show ticket_no AND name, as the first columns. I read this from the model's SQL (a model is not asked). Counts and breakdowns (an aggregate or a GROUP BY) are not about "a row per person" and are left alone. The pipeline gives the model ONE chance to fix it (first attempt only); I never refuse the answer over it.

doc: A question about a health check-up is about WHEN, so I treat a schedule row without its date as half an answer (and the person asked for the date). I judge it on the SQL: a list of rows from nlq.health_checkups must SELECT checkup_date. Counts and breakdowns are left alone.
